Rupee falls 9 paise to 94.50 against U.S. dollar in early trade
 At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 94.50 against the U.S. dollar, registering a fall of 9 paise from its previous close
 Updated - November 06, 2026 10:16 am IST - Mumbai 
 PTI READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 Image used for representational purposes only.
 | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto
 The rupee depreciated 9 paise to 94.50 against the U.S. dollar in early trade on Friday (November 6, 2026) as the broad strength of the American currency in the overseas market dented investor sentiment.
 Forex traders said overnight gains in crude oil prices and a recovery in the U.S. dollar weighed on the domestic unit.
 At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 94.50 against the U.S. dollar, registering a fall of 9 paise from its previous close.
 However, during initial trade, it recovered slightly to touch a high of 94.36 against the U.S. dollar.
 On Thursday (November 5), the rupee had settled at 94.41 against the American currency.
 The Bank of England kept policy rates unchanged while U.S. weekly unemployment claims were better than forecasts, said Anuj Choudhary, Research Analyst, Mirae Asset Sharekhan.
 "We expect the Rupee to trade with a positive bias on strength in domestic markets and fresh FII inflows," Mr. Choudhary said, adding that tensions between Ukraine and Russia and attacks in the West Asia may cap sharp upside.
 Meanwhile, the dollar index, which gauges the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was trading at 101.71, higher by 0.17%.
 Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading higher by 2.04% at $100.30 per barrel in futures trade.
 On the domestic equity market front, Sensex rose 33 points to 79,343.06 in early trade, while Nifty declined 52.95 points to 24,477.40.
 Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net buyers on Thursday (November 5), purchasing equities worth ₹14,974.68 crore, according to exchange data.
